function: CSI feedback: fully connected autoencoders compress angular-delay CSI at the UE and recover it at the BS, one subnetwork per channel zone selected by UE position (p. 2-3).
system: FDD massive MIMO, BS with 64-element UPA (16-by-4), single-antenna UE, OFDM, 3.5 GHz carrier; no RIS (p. 1, 4).
method: B fully connected autoencoder subnetworks (Table I), each trained independently on one channel cluster formed by UE position; end-to-end learning with MSE loss, compression rate 1/64 (p. 3-4).
data_channel: DeepMIMO Boston5G ray-tracing scenario, 3.5 GHz, 15 dominant paths; 105,996 UE channels, 24,000 for training and the remaining for testing (p. 4).
test_conditions: Trained on 24,000 channels, tested on the remaining samples of the same scenario; 8 zones versus 1 zone at rate 1/64; 10 km/h mobility for update rate (p. 4-5).
baselines: Single-zone versions of its own autoencoder (beta=16 and beta=128); no non-learned method and no published learned model compared, CsiNet [2] only cited (p. 4-5).
metrics: Channel NMSE (CDF over UEs, mean NMSE in dB); model parameters transmission rate and update rate (MPTR, MPUR); multiplications and parameters (p. 4-5).
complexity: Table II: 4,261,888 multiplications for 8-zone and small single-zone, 34,095,104 for large single-zone; parameter counts per model; encoder structure in Table I (p. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "we leverage the DeepMIMO Boston5G scenario [6]"
q2_support: p. 4: "samples are used for training the model and the remaining samples are for testing the model"
q3_support: p. 5: "feedback network for the entire site, with two model sizes"
q4_support: p. 5: "the number of multiplications that needs to be done in UE for each CSI feedback"
q5_support: p. 4: "we leverage the DeepMIMO Boston5G scenario [6]"
notes: PDF is arXiv:2401.07451v1 (5 pages), Zone-Specific CSI Feedback for Massive MIMO: A Situation-Aware Deep Learning Approach; it prints no DOI. q1 and q5 met through the public DeepMIMO Boston5G ray-tracing scenario; no link to the authors' own code is given. q2 not met: the test set is the held-out part of the same Boston5G data, and the 10 km/h mobility run only counts zone switches for MPUR (p. 5). q3 not met: the only comparators are single-zone variants of the proposed autoencoder (the method without zoning) and there is no non-learned method; CsiNet [2], TransNet [3] and CVLNet [4] are cited but not compared. q4 met by Table II (multiplications and parameters). Position-based zone selection by a classifier is part of the feedback scheme (p. 4), so the work is area 2.
